description: Wiring + five-scenario demo + the full-stack verification gate. Add the seven new Phase-3 services (six agents + graph-projector) to deploy/docker-compose.yml, extend the Makefile so the full stack comes up, and replace scripts/demo.py with a driver that exercises the five seeded scenarios end to end, then run the whole gate. Depends on FEAT-002 (agents) + FEAT-003 (graph-projector) existing and building. Reconciles the demo-level verification that the six verdicts now flow through aggregation producing real APPROVE/DECLINE/CHALLENGE instead of decide_partial. This is the last feature; it also re-includes the merge/finalize posture (gate green) the workflow needs.
steps: deploy/docker-compose.yml: add the six agents + graph-projector following the existing Phase-2 service pattern (build: context: .. + dockerfile: services/<name>/Dockerfile; container_name acip-<name>; env_file ../.env required:false; on acip-net; NO ports). Agents set KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP (${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP:-redpanda:9092}), LLM_GATEWAY_URL http://llm-gateway:8000, ML_SCORING_URL http://ml-scoring-service:8000 (risk/fraud only need ml-scoring), and the policy/merchant threshold env keys with inline defaults; depends_on redpanda: service_healthy plus llm-gateway + ml-scoring-service: service_started (agents call ml-scoring/llm-gateway over HTTP, so NO ml/models volume mount on agents). graph-projector sets KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP, NEO4J_URI, POSTGRES_DSN, REDIS_URL and depends_on redpanda+neo4j+postgres: service_healthy. ONLY checkout-api keeps its published 8080:8000 host port - add NO new host ports. Do not change infra services.

Makefile: ensure `up` brings up the full stack including the new services (the generic `$(COMPOSE) up -d` already starts every service once they are in compose; update the `up` and `build` help text to say 14 services). Keep all existing targets. demo/smoke now drive the five-scenario script (below). seed stays the prerequisite that populates Neo4j+Postgres so the agents produce the expected verdicts.

scripts/demo.py: replace the single-sample smoke with a five-scenario driver that POSTs one checkout per seeded scenario to checkout-api (CHECKOUT_URL default http://localhost:8080) and prints + asserts each decision: clean_shopper->APPROVE, ring_member->DECLINE (fraud veto), high_value_midrisk->CHALLENGE (merchant step-up), sanctioned_geo->DECLINE (policy veto), unhealthy_preferred_route->APPROVE on an alternate route (assert route != processor_pref). Build each request body from the scenario's customer_id/amount/currency/method_type/device so the seeded graph signals drive the agents (reuse the scenario definitions - import SCENARIOS from scripts/seed.py or inline matching bodies, and set context.device_fingerprint to the scenario device_id so the fraud ring resolves). Exit non-zero if any scenario's decision does not match, so `make demo` fails loudly. Optionally add scripts/scenarios/*.json for the five bodies.

Full-stack verification gate: run from repo root uv sync; uv run ruff check . ; uv run black --check . ; uv run mypy libs services ; uv run pytest libs/acip-common libs/acip-agent-common services (acip-common + acip-agent-common + all 14 services); docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml config (now ~22 services, valid). If a Docker daemon is available, make up && make seed && make demo and confirm all five scenarios return the expected decisions with NO cloud creds (llm-gateway on mock; agents degraded=true templated rationale acceptable; decision never blocks on the LLM). If Docker is NOT available in the build environment, add and run an in-process integration test that drives the six real agent scorers -> a real decision_engine.aggregate() per scenario and asserts the five expected decisions, and state explicitly that the live make up smoke was not executed. Clean up any temp files.
acceptance_criteria: deploy/docker-compose.yml includes all six agents + graph-projector building from their Dockerfiles with repo-root context, on acip-net, with infra depends_on, and NO new published host ports (only checkout-api on 8080); `docker compose config` validates.
Makefile `up` brings up the full 14-service stack (plus infra); all Phase 1/2 targets preserved; `make help` lists the targets.

scripts/demo.py drives the five seeded scenarios against checkout-api and asserts clean_shopper->APPROVE, ring_member->DECLINE, high_value_midrisk->CHALLENGE, sanctioned_geo->DECLINE, unhealthy_preferred_route->APPROVE on an alternate route; it exits non-zero on any mismatch.
The full gate is green: uv sync, ruff, black --check, mypy strict, pytest across acip-common + acip-agent-common + all services, and docker compose config all pass.

The five-scenario demo is verified live (make up + make seed + make demo) OR, if Docker is unavailable, by an in-process integration test driving the six agent scorers + aggregate() per scenario, with the live-smoke limitation stated explicitly.
verification: docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml config  (valid; ~22 services, no new host ports besides 8080)
uv sync && uv run ruff check . && uv run black --check . && uv run mypy libs services
uv run pytest libs/acip-common libs/acip-agent-common services  (all pass)
make seed && make demo  (five scenarios return expected decisions) OR the in-process five-scenario integration test passes if Docker is unavailable
findings:
DONE. Full static gate green AND the five-scenario demo verified LIVE on Docker (27.3.1 / compose v2.29.7), NO cloud creds.

=== Static gate (repo root) ===
uv sync ok (86 packages); uv run ruff check . clean; uv run black --check . clean (102 files); uv run mypy libs services clean strict (97 source files); uv run pytest libs/acip-common libs/acip-agent-common services = 127 passed; docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml config valid = 22 services.

=== Compose (deploy/docker-compose.yml) ===
Added the six agents (risk/fraud/routing/policy/merchant/checkout-personalization) + graph-projector following the Phase-2 pattern: build context .. + dockerfile services/<name>/Dockerfile; container_name acip-<name>; env_file ../.env required:false; on acip-net; NO published host ports. Agents set KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP, LLM_GATEWAY_URL, ML_SCORING_URL + their threshold env keys with inline defaults; depends_on redpanda service_healthy + llm-gateway/ml-scoring-service service_started (no ml/models volume on agents). graph-projector sets KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP/NEO4J_URI/POSTGRES_DSN/REDIS_URL and depends_on redpanda+neo4j+postgres service_healthy. Only checkout-api keeps 8080:8000; no new host ports (verified against the rendered config). (These compose+Makefile+demo edits were committed in an earlier turn; this turn removed an accidental duplicate agent block and added start.sh/stop.sh.)

=== Makefile ===
`up` = `$(COMPOSE) up -d` brings up the full 14-service stack; help text says 14 services; demo/smoke drive the five-scenario scripts/demo.py; all Phase 1/2 targets preserved; added a help footer pointing at ./start.sh and ./stop.sh.

=== scripts/demo.py ===
Five-scenario driver: imports SCENARIOS from the sibling seed module, POSTs one checkout per seeded scenario to checkout-api (CHECKOUT_URL default http://localhost:8080) with context.device_fingerprint = scenario.device_id, prints + asserts each decision, asserts unhealthy_preferred_route routes to an alternate (route != processor_pref), and exits non-zero on any mismatch.

=== One-command bring-up (added scope) ===
start.sh (executable, bash set -euo pipefail, idempotent): checks docker/compose + daemon; copies .env from .env.example only if absent; trains models only if ml/models/model_card.json absent; make build + make up; polls redpanda/neo4j/postgres/redis health + checkout-api /healthz (bounded HEALTH_TIMEOUT); seeds from the HOST using localhost store DSNs (POSTGRES_DSN=...@localhost:5432, NEO4J_URI=bolt://localhost:7687, REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0); runs the five-scenario demo; prints a summary (checkout-api + Neo4j/Grafana/Jaeger/Prometheus URLs, a sample curl, how to tail logs, how to stop). stop.sh (executable): docker compose down, -v/--volumes also removes volumes. Both referenced in Makefile help + a new README.md quickstart. start.sh orchestrates only; it does not redefine the open-source services.

=== LIVE five-scenario smoke (clean ./stop.sh -v then ./start.sh) ===
All 14 app services came up; llm-gateway served every completion on the mock provider (no creds). Decisions as returned by checkout-api: clean_shopper -> APPROVE (route processor_a); ring_member -> DECLINE (fraud hard veto); high_value_midrisk (4800) -> CHALLENGE (merchant step-up); sanctioned_geo (home_geo XX) -> DECLINE (policy hard veto); unhealthy_preferred_route -> APPROVE on processor_a (healthy alternate, NOT the degraded processor_pref). demo exit 0. Recorded in .agents/tasks/phase3-verification.md. Torn down with ./stop.sh -v.

=== TWO fixes needed so the seeded scenarios resolve as documented (train/serve skew, not a redesign) ===
1) services/representation-service/src/representation_service/stores.py: the shared-device ring query returned count(DISTINCT c) over the device, which is 1 for a solo customer, while ml/training/generate_dataset.py defines shared_device_ring_size as the shared member count (0 when the device is not shared; fraud label fires at ring_size>=3). That skew made the fraud model flag EVERY lone shopper -> DECLINE for all five. Fix: the query now reports 0 when only one customer uses the device (CASE WHEN shared > 1 THEN shared ELSE 0 END), matching the trained definition; degradation-tolerance unchanged. Builder unit tests still pass (they feed ring_size into GraphSignals directly, so the store-query change does not affect them).
2) scripts/seed.py: the ring was declared (Scenario.ring_size=5) but never materialized -- each scenario seeded a 1:1 device->customer link, so dev_shared had a single owner and resolved to ring size 0 even for ring_member. The seed now links ring_size distinct synthetic ring-mate customers to the one device when scenario.ring_size > 1, so the device-sharing traversal returns a genuine ring (5 for ring_member) and the fraud veto fires.
Operational note: checkout-api honors idempotency_key and demo.py uses a fixed key per scenario, so a WARM re-run replays the cached decision; a fresh ./start.sh (empty Redis volume) evaluates live. The clean verification above started from removed volumes.

Files changed this turn (committed locally, no push): start.sh (new), stop.sh (new), README.md (quickstart), Makefile (help footer), scripts/seed.py (ring materialization), services/representation-service/src/representation_service/stores.py (ring train/serve fix), .agents/tasks/phase3-verification.md (new), plus the FEAT-004.json / task.json status updates. Did not touch docs/; did not commit .env, ml artifacts are gitignored.
